title: Seqlen spectrum fusion: micro-batch compactor for padding reduction
creator: Alyssa Hartmann
description:
Background: Our production token cost is dominated by wasted compute from padding when micro-batches contain heterogeneous sequence lengths. This ticket proposes a lightweight runtime component — the 'Seqlen Spectrum Compactor' — that fuses requests by mapping sequence lengths to a compact spectrum, applies quantile-based bucketing, and performs targeted micro-batch reshaping before kernel selection. The goal is to reduce padded tokens across prefill and decode phases while maintaining latency SLOs and keeping scheduling overhead < 200us per batch.

Scope: prototype algorithm in the serving runtime for per-GPU request coalescing, integration points for kernel-hint annotations, fallbacks to existing bucketers, and perf guardrails (max reorder latency, head-of-line fairness). Not included: model-level accuracy regressions, frontend API changes, or autoscaling policies.

Success metrics: 10-20% reduction in padded tokens for mixed-seq workloads in our synthetic traces, tail latency (p95/p99) within 10% of baseline, and <5% throughput regression for high-concurrency steady-state.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented compactor integrated into runtime with feature flag
Quantile-bucketing strategy implemented and configurable (num buckets, quantile thresholds)
End-to-end benchmarks showing padded token reduction >= 10% on three representative workloads
Latency SLOs: p95 increase <= 10%, p99 increase <= 15% across test harness
Kernel hint metadata emitted to selection layer; runtime falls back when hint incompatible
Unit and integration tests for compactor logic and correctness guards
tasks: Design quantile-spectrum mapping and bucket merge heuristics (Alyssa)
Implement lightweight histogram estimator for incoming request window (Diego)
Micro-batch reshaper that preserves arrival order constraints up to configurable reorder_budget
Emit kernel-hint annotations (preferred kernel, estimated effective seqlen) to scheduler
Integrate with KV-prefill logic to avoid double-counting cached prefix tokens
Perf harness: generate mixed-length traces, run before/after compare on dedicated GPU pool
PR for runtime changes, include feature flag and telemetry (padded_tokens, reshuffle_rate, reorder_latency)
Rollout plan and rollback criteria documented in runtime-1.19 release notes
comments: 2026-02-12 Alyssa Hartmann: Initial write-up with motivation and high-level approach. Posted draft to #runtime-arch for upstream feedback.

2026-02-18 Diego Martinez: Spike completed — prototype histogram estimator looks stable on local traces. Observed ~14% pad reduction on mixed-chat workload but p99 increased +9% under one stress pattern. Need guard on max-reorder-time.

2026-02-23 Victor Chen (review): Great direction. Two concerns: (1) interaction with prefill KV cache — reshaping must not invalidate cache reuse heuristics, (2) kernel-selection compatibility when compactor forces unusual batch shapes. Suggest emitting kernel hints and conservative fallback.
2026-03-01 Alyssa Hartmann: Updated acceptance criteria to require kernel-hint emission and fallback behaviour. Added reorder_budget parameter to tasks.

2026-03-05 QA (Rina S.): Perf harness added. Running larger-scale jobs this week. Observed cases where compaction increased throughput but hurt tail latency for tiny short-live requests (chat tokens). Adding opt-out label for latency-sensitive route.

2026-03-10 Diego Martinez: Merged spike branch to feature/compactor (internal). Opening PR for review: runtime/compactor-v1. Plumbed telemetry counters: padded_tokens_saved, compaction_rate, reorder_latency_p90. Requesting design review and kernel-scheduler review before canary rollout.
